questions.text: What does Nursultan Akhanov study at WKU?
questions.hint: "I study Economics at WKU — it is my second year and I enjoy it very much." — Nursultan.

questions.text: Nursultan earned his entire 15,000-tenge budget through his tutoring job.
questions.hint: "5,000 from my monthly allowance, 7,000 from a part-time tutoring job, and 3,000 that my parents sent for my birthday." — three sources, not one.

questions.text: What did the market seller give Nursultan for free?
questions.hint: "The seller offered to give me a small bag of walnuts for free because I bought two things." — a reward for buying both apples and apricots.

questions.text: The hardcover edition of the economics book cost ___ tenge — too expensive for Nursultan's budget.
questions.hint: "The first was a hardcover edition... It was beautiful, but it cost 3,500 tenge." — so he chose the 1,800-tenge paperback instead.

questions.text: Why did Nursultan choose the blue phone case instead of the cheaper black one?
opts: The black case was out of stock
The blue case was on sale
The blue case had a WKU logo on the back
The black case was the wrong size for his phone
questions.correct: The blue case had a WKU logo on the back
questions.hint: "It was a dark blue silicone case with a small WKU logo printed on the back... I preferred the blue one with the logo."

questions.text: Nursultan paid for the phone case in cash.
questions.hint: "I paid the 2,500 tenge BY CARD." — he paid by card, not cash. He asked about cheaper options first, then paid by card.

questions.text: Nursultan bought a red scarf as a birthday gift for his sister ___.
questions.hint: "My sister AIGERIM was turning seventeen in two weeks... She loves red, and the winters in Karagandy are very cold."

questions.text: How much money did Nursultan have left after all his purchases on Saturday?
questions.hint: "15,000 − 11,450 = 3,550 tenge. I walked home feeling satisfied — and already planning what to do with my 3,550 tenge next weekend."

questions.text: Who are Sanzhar and Asel buying a gift for?
questions.hint: "How much is that photo frame? I think our PROFESSOR would really like it." — They are choosing a group gift for their professor.

questions.text: The photo frame in the gift shop costs 3,200 tenge.
questions.hint: "Let me check the price tag... it says 3,200 tenge." — Sanzhar reads the price aloud. 3,200 tenge — confirmed.

questions.text: The total cost of the pen set and the bookmarks together is ___ tenge.
questions.hint: "The pen set plus bookmarks is 2,550 tenge total." — 2,100 (pen set) + 450 (bookmarks) = 2,550 tenge.

questions.text: What is the exchange rate at Uralsk City Bank on the day Tolegen visits?
questions.hint: "Today's rate is 460 tenge to one dollar. So fifty dollars gives you 23,000 tenge." — the bank teller explains clearly.

questions.text: The bank charges a commission of two percent for the currency exchange.
questions.hint: "Our commission is ONE percent." — Not two, but ONE percent. 1% of 23,000 = 230 tenge commission.

questions.text: How much does a domestic transfer cost if the amount is under 50,000 tenge?
questions.hint: "A domestic transfer costs 150 tenge if the amount is under 50,000 tenge." — 300 tenge is for amounts ABOVE 50,000.

questions.text: Which is the correct spelling of the number 40?
questions.hint: 40 = FORTY — the "u" from "four" disappears: four → forty. ❌ "fourty" is the most common mistake in English. F-O-R-T-Y.

questions.text: Write the number 350 in English words: "three hundred and ___".
questions.hint: 350 = three hundred AND fifty. 50 = FIFTY (not "fivety"!). five → fifty. AND is required between the hundreds and the remainder.

questions.text: How do you correctly say the price 2,500 tenge in English?
opts: two thousand and five hundred tenge
questions.hint: 2,500 = TWO THOUSAND FIVE HUNDRED tenge. No -s on "thousand" or "hundred"! "Twenty-five hundred" is American English — use "two thousand five hundred" at WKU.

questions.text: "I'll pay by cash" is the correct English phrase for paying with physical money.
questions.hint: Correct: "I'll pay IN cash" (наличными → предлог IN). "I'll pay BY card" (картой → предлог BY). ❌ "by cash" is wrong — must be IN cash!

questions.text: The hardcover book costs 3,500 tenge. The paperback costs 1,800 tenge. Which sentence is correct?
opts: The paperback is more cheaper than the hardcover.
The hardcover is cheaper than the paperback.
The paperback is cheaper than the hardcover.
The hardcover is the most cheap option.
questions.correct: The paperback is cheaper than the hardcover.
questions.hint: cheap → CHEAPER (short adjective → -er, NOT "more cheaper"!). 1,800 < 3,500, so the paperback IS cheaper. ✅

questions.text: Complete the question: "How ___ is it?" — the most common way to ask for a price.
questions.hint: "How MUCH is it?" — the universal question for asking a price in English. "How much does it cost?" is also correct but less natural in a shop.

questions.text: Aigerim's birthday is on the ___ of March — which ordinal number completes this for the 17th?
questions.hint: 17th = SEVENTEENTH. Ordinal numbers are used for dates: 1st=first, 2nd=second, 3rd=third, 17th=seventeenth. Never use the basic number "seventeen" for dates!

questions.text: "I received three hundreds tenge as change" is correct English.
questions.hint: HUNDRED never takes -s when used with a number! ❌ "three hundreds" → ✅ "three hundred." Same rule: "two thousand" ✅ "two thousands" ❌.

questions.text: What does "bargain" mean?
opts: Something bought for less than its usual price
A type of discount card for students
The price written on a label in a shop
questions.correct: Something bought for less than its usual price
questions.hint: "The pen set and bookmarks for 2,550 tenge shared by eight people — that's a real BARGAIN!" A bargain = great value for the price.

questions.text: "Commission" is extra money that a bank GIVES you as a reward for using their services.
questions.hint: COMMISSION = a fee the bank TAKES from you for handling a transaction. "Our commission is 1% — so we take 230 tenge from your 23,000." It is a cost, not a reward!

questions.text: The money you receive back when you pay more than the exact price is called ___.
questions.hint: CHANGE = сдача. "We paid 2,700 tenge for a 2,550-tenge item. The CHANGE is 150 tenge." · "Keep the change." · "Do you have change for 1,000 tenge?"

questions.text: What does "split" mean in the sentence "Let's split the cost between eight people"?
opts: To hide part of the cost from others
To pay the entire cost yourself
To divide the cost equally between people
To argue about who should pay more
questions.correct: To divide the cost equally between people
questions.hint: "If eight people SPLIT the cost, that's about 319 tenge each." SPLIT = to divide equally. "Split the bill" is a very common phrase in English.

questions.text: What does "on sale" mean?
opts: A product that is very popular and hard to find
An item sold at a higher price than usual
Something being sold at a reduced price for a limited time
A product that is available to buy online only
questions.correct: Something being sold at a reduced price for a limited time
questions.hint: "The jacket was ON SALE for 8,000 tenge — originally 10,000." ON SALE = со скидкой, цена снижена. A temporary reduced price.

questions.text: "Savings" refers to money you spend regularly on food, transport, and study materials.
questions.hint: SAVINGS = money you KEEP and do not spend — money put aside for the future. "He kept his SAVINGS in a separate digital account." The opposite of savings is expenses (расходы).

questions.text: "I spend about 7,000 tenge on food — this is not exact, it is an ___ figure."
questions.hint: APPROXIMATE = приблизительный. "I spend an APPROXIMATE amount of 7,000 tenge on food." Not exact, but close. Adverb: "approximately 7,000 tenge."

questions.text: What does "value" mean in "the paperback was better value for money"?
opts: The physical weight of the item
How much something is worth compared to its price
The discount you receive at the checkout
The original price before any reduction
questions.correct: How much something is worth compared to its price
questions.hint: "The paperback was better VALUE — same content as the hardcover, but for 1,800 instead of 3,500." VALUE = quality or usefulness you get for the price you pay.
